issues.description: Test was patched with a zero-amount/zero-puzzle-hash Addition to satisfy new validation, masking a breaking change to the empty-additions contract
issues.detail: Old cat_spend accepted additions=[] and fell back to amount/inner_address. New code forwards request.additions directly, so empty list now fails CreateSignedTransaction.__post_init__. Rather than preserving prior semantics, the test feeds a junk Addition. Real callers passing additions=[] will break. Either keep additions=[] equivalent to None, or document the breakage explicitly.

issues.description: CreateSignedTransaction is accreting CAT-specific and puzzle_decorator fields with an apology comment instead of a clean design
issues.detail: extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution, and puzzle_decorator are now on a generic request with a comment admitting the puzzle_decorator typing is 'a slight hack' supporting only Clawback. Either enforce the constraint in the type system (nested CatDiscrepancy value, discriminated union for the decorator) or split the endpoints. Shipping a generic field with an apology is the worst of both options.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation ships three type: ignore comments and a 'None in {...}' set-membership trick as a public helper
issues.detail: The function admits mypy 'doesn't see the elif'. Fix it with explicit None checks or assertions after the elif and remove the ignores. Also rewrite the clever 'None in {a,b,c}' as 'any(x is None for x in (...))' to state the invariant plainly. Tolerable buried in a property; not tolerable as a shared helper.

issues.description: send_transaction silently swapped its prefix-check error contract for ensure_valid_address
issues.detail: The old code rejected with 'Unexpected Address Prefix'. The new code calls ensure_valid_address with allowed_types={AddressType.XCH}, which raises a different message and may accept/reject different inputs. A refactor that changes user-visible error contracts is a behavior change, not a refactor. Preserve the message or call it out in the commit.

issues.description: send_transaction and cat_spend discard get_wallet's return value with only '# opportunity to raise' as explanation
issues.detail: The call exists purely for its side effect of raising. Extract a named validate_wallet_id(id, required_type) helper or write an explicit comment stating the invariant. 'Opportunity to raise' reads like the author was unsure. Also note create_signed_transaction likely looks up the wallet again — confirm this isn't a redundant double lookup.

issues.description: Diff bundles refactor, new fields, behavior changes, and test edits in one commit, hurting bisectability
issues.detail: Extracting cat_discrepancy_validation, adding CAT fields to CreateSignedTransaction, forwarding send_transaction and cat_spend, and plumbing puzzle_decorator_override/cat_discrepancy in _generate_signed_transaction are four independent patches. Bisecting a regression here requires reading the whole diff. Split into sequential commits so each change is reviewable and revertable on its own.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR has the right intent — collapsing send_transaction and cat_spend onto create_signed_transaction — but the execution complects concerns and quietly changes public behavior. The unanimous P0 is the test edit feeding a junk zero-amount Addition to satisfy new validation, which masks a regression for callers passing additions=[]. CreateSignedTransaction is accreting CAT-specific fields with an admitted hack instead of a clean decomposition, and the new shared cat_discrepancy_validation helper ships with three type: ignore comments that should be fixed. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — preserve the public API, decompose the request type, clean the helper, and split the diff.
